requested_changes.body:
There exists a `MissingDependencyException` error in botocore that we usually throw for cases when we're missing CRT or don't have a minimum supported version. I think we should do one of the following:
- Use `MissingDependencyException`
- Have `MissingMinimumCrtVersionError` inherit from `MissingDependencyException` so people catching these types of exceptions don't have to try and catch a new one

comments.body:
Ideally, validation would occur when the CRT request args are being built in s3transfer since technically the config values could be changed after creating the CRT transfer manager. The reason I'm not doing that right now is because s3transfer doesn't have knowledge of boto3's transfer config aliases, `max_concurrency` and `max_io_queue`.

I'm wondering if, for aliases, we use the alias values as the ground truth when performing validation (ie `max_request_concurrency` and `max_io_queue_size`.
- s3transfer has knowledge of these config properties.
- boto3's `TransferConfig` will always set values for alias keys and values when setting an alias key. But will only set the alias value when setting the alias value. So for example:
  - `config.max_concurrency = 10` sets both `max_concurrency` and `max_request_concurrency`
  - But `config.max_request_concurrency = 10` only sets `max_request_concurrency`.

If we always take the alias value as the param to validate on, then we can move this logic to s3transfer.

comments.body:
Looking at https://github.com/boto/s3transfer/pull/361, it seems like `multipart_chunksize`, `multipart_threshold`, and `preferred_transfer_client` are the config options that we actually use for CRT.

Why are `max_concurrency` and `max_request_concurrency` allowed if they never get passed to the CRT? Or where do they get passed?

So we're currently checking for a minimum supported version of v0.19.18 for `awscrt`. I think there are some requirements we're waiting on from a new version of CRT for the new `crt` option. Does this need its own min version check or is v0.19.18 good enough?
